mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction triggers a decline in equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat despite the rate spike, or FEDFUNDS does not revert within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in hourly wage growth (indirect via UNRATE) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investor sentiment deteriorates.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the prior 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) during such labor conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month average for three consecutive months predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as a leading indicator of economic expansion.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when INDPRO is above threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months suggests a disinflationary environment that supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL remaining below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of RSAFS to GDP (implied liquidity) falls below 0.8, it indicates excess liquidity, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS / GDPC1 < 0.8 in the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive or are statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in unemployment (PAYEMS) by more than 5,000 in a month predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to increased risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5,000 in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS below 4.0% for 4 consecutive months signals a prolonged easing phase, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month FEDFUNDS MA crosses and stays below 4.0% for 4 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 4-week moving average of industrial production (INDPRO) falls below its 52-week high, it indicates softening demand, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such declines.
